readings.title: A Foolish and Rebellious People
readings.subtitle: Their sins have kept good things from them.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 5:20] <dq>“Declare this in the house of Ya‛aqoḇ and proclaim it in Yehuḏah, saying,</dq>
[21] <dq>Hear this now, O foolish people without heart, who have eyes and see not, and who have ears and hear not:</dq>
[22] <dq>Do you not fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>Me</dn>?’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>‘Do you not tremble at <dn>My</dn> presence, who have placed the sand as the boundary of the sea, by an everlasting law, and it does not pass over it? Though its waves toss to and fro, they are not able; though they roar, they do not pass over it.</dq>
[23] <dq>But this people has a backsliding and rebellious heart, they have turned aside and gone away.</dq>
[24] <dq>And they do not say in their heart, “Let us now fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, who gives rain, both the former and the latter, in its season. <dn>He</dn> guards for us, the required-by>-law, weeks of the harvest.”</dq>
[25] <dq>Your crookednesses have turned these away, and your sins have kept the good from you.</dq>
[26] <dq>For among <dn>My</dn> people are found wrong men who lie in wait as one who sets snares. They have set up a trap, they catch men.</dq>
[27] <dq>As a cage is filled with birds, so their houses are filled with deceit. Therefore they have become great and grown rich.</dq>
[28] <dq>They have become fat, they are sleek. They also overlook the deeds of the wrong. They did not rightly rule the cause of the fatherless, so that they prosper. And the right of the needy they did not rightly rule.</dq>
[29] <dq>Would <dn>I</dn> not punish them for this?’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>‘Would <dn>I</dn> not revenge <dn>Myself</dn> on such a nation as this?’</dq>
[30] <dq>“An astounding and horrible matter has come to be in the land:</dq>
[31] <dq>The prophets have prophesied falsely, and the priests rule by their own hand, and <dn>My</dn> people have loved it so. And what are you going to do at the end of it?</dq>

readings.title: Flee from Jerusalem
readings.subtitle: Evil appears from the north, and great destruction.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 6:1] “O children of Binyamin, gather yourselves to flee out of the midst of Yerushalayim! Blow a shophar in Teqova, and set up a signal-fire in Běyth Hakkerem, for evil has been seen from the north, and great destruction.
[2] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall cut off the lovely and delicate one, the daughter of Tsiyon.</dq>
[3] <dq>“The shepherds with their flocks shall come to her, they shall pitch their tents against her all around. They shall pasture, each one in his own place.”</dq>
[4] “Set apart battle against her. Arise, and let us go up at noon. Woe to us, for the day goes away, for the shadows of the evening are lengthening.
[5] “Arise, and let us go by night, and let us destroy her palaces.”
[6] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“Cut down her trees, and cast up a siege mound against Yerushalayim. She is the city to be punished, in whose midst there is only oppression.</dq>
[7] <dq>“As a well flows with water, so she flows with her evil. Violence and destruction are heard in her. Before <dn>Me</dn> continually are suffering and smiting.</dq>
[8] <dq>“Be instructed, O Yerushalayim, lest <dn>My</dn> being be torn from you, lest <dn>I</dn> make you a waste, a land not inhabited.”</dq>
[9] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“Let them thoroughly glean as a vine <dn>את</dn> the remnant of Yisra’ěl; pass your hand again over the branches like a grape-gatherer.”</dq>

readings.title: Uncircumcised Ears
readings.subtitle: They cry 'Peace, peace,' when there is no peace.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 6:10] To whom shall <dn>I</dn> speak and give warning, so that they hear? See, their ear is uncircumcised, and they are unable to listen. See, the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is a reproach to them, they do not delight in it.
[11] Therefore <dn>I</dn> am filled with the wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dn>I</dn> have become weary of containing it. <dq>“Pour it out on the children outside, and on the company of young men together, for even husband and wife shall be taken, the aged and the very old.</dq>
[12] <dq>“And their houses shall be turned over to others, fields and wives together. For <dn>I</dn> shall stretch out <dn>My</dn> hand against the inhabitants of the land,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[13] <dq>“For from the least of them even to the greatest of them, they are all greedy for gain. And from the prophet even to the priest, all act falsely.</dq>
[14] <dq>“And they heal the breach of <dn>My</dn> people slightly, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there is no peace.</dq>
[15] <dq>Were they ashamed when they had done abomination? No! They were not at all ashamed, nor did they know how to blush. Therefore they shall fall among those who fall. They shall stumble at the time <dn>I</dn> visit them,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: Rejection of the Ancient Paths
readings.subtitle: Your ascending offerings are not acceptable.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 6:16] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Stand in the ways and see, and ask for the old paths, where the good way is, and walk in it; and find rest for yourselves. But they said, ‘We do not walk in it.’</dq>
[17] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> raised up watchmen over you, and said, ‘Listen to a voice of a shophar!’ But they said, ‘We do not listen.’</dq>
[18] <dq>“Therefore hear, you nations, and know, O congregation, what is upon them!</dq>
[19] <dq>“Hear, O earth! See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing evil upon this people, even the fruit of their thoughts, because they have not listened to <dn>My</dn> words, nor <dn>My</dn> Torah – and they rejected it.</dq>
[20] <dq>“What need have <dn>I</dn> of frankincense from Sheḇa, and sweet cane from a distant land? Your ascending offerings are not acceptable, and your slaughterings have not been sweet to <dn>Me</dn>.”</dq>
[21] Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am laying stumbling-blocks before this people. And the fathers and the sons together shall stumble on them, the neighbour and his friend shall perish.”</dq>

readings.title: The Invader from the North
readings.subtitle: They shall be called rejected silver.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 6:22] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, a people shall come from the land of the north, and a great nation is stirred up from the farthest parts of the earth,</dq>
[23] <dq>they strengthen their bow and spear, they are cruel and have no compassion, their voice roars like the sea. And they ride on horses, set in array as a man for battle against you, O daughter of Tsiyon.”</dq>
[24] We have heard the report of it, our hands grow weak. Distress has taken hold of us, pain as of a woman in labour.
[25] Do not go out into the field, nor walk by the way. Because of the sword of the enemy, fear is on every side.
[26] O daughter of my people, gird on sackcloth, and roll about in ashes! Make mourning as for an only son, most bitter lamentation because suddenly the ravager shall come upon us.
[27] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have made you a trier and a stronghold among <dn>My</dn> people, so that you know, and shall try their way.</dq>
[28] <dq>“All of them are rebels of rebels, walking as slanderers. They are bronze and iron, all of them are corrupters.</dq>
[29] <dq>“The bellows have burned, the lead has been consumed by fire. The refiner has refined in vain, for those who are evil have not been separated.</dq>
[30] <dq>“They shall call them rejected silver, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has rejected them.”</dq>

readings.title: The Book of the Torah Found
readings.subtitle: Hilkiah the priest finds the book during temple repairs.
readings.text:
[2 Kings 22:3] And it came to be, in the eighteenth year of Sovereign Yoshiyahu, that the sovereign sent <dn>את</dn> Shaphan the scribe, son of Atsalyahu, son of Meshullam, to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying,
[4] “Go up to Ḥilqiyahu the high priest, and let him weigh <dn>את</dn> the silver which has been brought into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which the doorkeepers have gathered from the people.
[5] “And let them give it into the hand of those doing the work, who are the overseers in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And let them give it to those who are in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> doing the work, to strengthen the breach of the house,
[6] to carpenters and to builders and to stonemasons, and to buy timber and hewn stone to strengthen the house.
[7] “However, let not the silver given into their hand be reckoned with <dn>את</dn> them, for they are acting trustworthily.”
[8] And Ḥilqiyahu the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe, “<dn>I</dn> have found <dn>את</dn> the Book of the Torah in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” And Ḥilqiyah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.
[9] And Shaphan the scribe came to the sovereign, and brought word to the sovereign again, saying, “Your servants have gathered the silver that was found in the house, and have given it into the hand of those who do the work, who oversee the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”
[10] And Shaphan the scribe informed the sovereign, saying, “Ḥilqiyah the priest has given me a book.” And Shaphan read it before the sovereign.
[11] And it came to be, when the sovereign heard <dn>את</dn> the words of the Book of the Torah, that he tore his garments,

readings.title: Huldah's Prophecy
readings.subtitle: Josiah humbles himself and is spared from seeing the coming disaster.
readings.text:
[2 Kings 22:12] and the sovereign commanded <dn>את</dn> Ḥilqiyah the priest, and <dn>את</dn> Aḥiqam son of Shaphan, and <dn>את</dn> Aḵbor son of Miḵayah, and <dn>את</dn> Shaphan the scribe, and <dn>את</dn> Asayah a servant of the sovereign, saying,
[13] “Go, inquire of <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for me, for the people and for all Yehuḏah, concerning the words of this book that has been found. For great is the wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not obeyed the words of this book, to do according to all that is written concerning us.”
[14] Then Ḥilqiyahu the priest, and Aḥiqam, and Aḵbor, and Shaphan, and Asayah went to Ḥuldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Tiqvah, son of Ḥarḥas, keeper of the wardrobe. Now she was dwelling in Yerushalayim in the Second Quarter. And they spoke with her.
[15] And she said to them, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, ‘Say to the man who sent you to <dn>Me</dn>,
[16] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing evil on this place and on its inhabitants, all the words of the book which the sovereign of Yehuḏah has read,</dq>
[17] <dq>because they have forsaken <dn>Me</dn> and burned incense to other mighty ones to provoke <dn>Me</dn> with all the works of their hands. And so <dn>My</dn> wrath shall be kindled against this place and not be quenched.’ ” ’</dq>
[18] “And to the sovereign of Yehuḏah, who sent you to inquire of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, say this to him, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“As for the words which you have heard,</dq>
[19] <dq>because your heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> when you heard <dn>את</dn> what <dn>I</dn> spoke against this place and against its inhabitants, that they would become a ruin and a curse, and did tare your garments and wept before <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> also have heard,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[20] <dq>“Therefore, see, <dn>I</dn> am gathering you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your burial-site in peace, so that your eyes do not see all the evil <dn>I</dn> am bringing on this place.” ’ ”</dq> And they brought word to the sovereign.
